clue.text: Was inclined, having served clumsily, to withdraw quietly

indicators.note: to withdraw something is to take it away, so the quiet letter is pulled out of the verb

parts.note: to slop food is to serve it out messily, slopping it onto the plate
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone who fancied a go, botched their serve on court and then crept off without a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to withdraw' takes P out of SLOPPED. 'having' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping ground leans at an angle, so a surface that leant or tilted can be said to have done this.

clue.text: Not a very busy period, but one gets a long way

definitions.meaning: a year with little work in it, an easy twelve months
a unit of astronomical distance, which travels very far

explanation.surface: A quiet year at work, yet one still makes great progress.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a slack twelve months and the distance travelled by a beam in twelve months.

clue.text: Clergyman even a little early?

parts.note: split as ..., the word means before being late, i.e. early; whole, it is a bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman who turns up just ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two parts, the word means before late; whole, it is a senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop or abbot is a high-ranking churchman, a senior member of the clergy.

clue.text: Perhaps man in Cardiff finds platform short

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the final letter of the stage is dropped

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform

explanation.surface: A Welshman discovers the stage he's on falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardiff is the capital of Wales; 'Perhaps' marks the name as an example of a Welsh man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a typical Welsh first name, a form of David, so an example of a Welshman.

clue.text: Recover from exercise, with fingers at side?

parts.note: with your fingertips by your side, your limb is hanging low: an arm, down

explanation.surface: An instruction for cooling off after a workout, standing with hands loose by the hips.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'fingers at side' describes a posture rather than giving a word directly.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle routine of easy stretching after sport lets the body cool and return to rest, the opposite of the opening routine.

clue.text: Carries on making money

definitions.meaning: to carry on a war or campaign is to conduct it

explanation.surface: Someone continues earning a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for conducting a campaign and the regular pay earned by workers.

clue.text: Prompt attention secures fibres for such clothes

indicators.note: secures means holds in place, so the two words close round the fibres

parts.note: ready means prompt, quick to act
to lend an ear is to pay attention
tow is coarse flax or hemp fibre

explanation.surface: Quick care fastens the threads of off-the-peg garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-peg garments are made in standard sizes to buy and put on at once, not tailored.

clue.text: Almost rainless? Nothing much more than that

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is left off

parts.note: a rainless spell is dry
ought is an old word for nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A weather report: barely any rain, and no more than that.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back to the first word: far beyond merely rainless.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spell without any rain goes well beyond a dry day, a prolonged shortage of water.

clue.text: Thoroughly comfy to the end in wet-weather gear

parts.note: well means thoroughly, as in well mixed

indicators.note: going to the end of the word means taking only its final letter

explanation.surface: Boots that stay cosy all the way down to the toes in the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a joining word. A welly is a British rubber boot (wellington).
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber boots worn in rain and mud are a classic item of rainy-day clothing.

clue.text: At one, no time for a welcome

indicators.note: no here means without, so a letter is dropped from the word that follows

parts.note: a welcome is a greeting given to someone arriving

explanation.surface: Someone at one with the world too busy to bother with a hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a joining word: A, then GREETING less its T.
explanation.definitionFit: People at one are united in opinion, in accord with each other.

clue.text: Divine figure with a halo on head?

indicators.note: on in a down-style reading places the ring after the head, so it is written second

parts.note: poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax charged per head
a halo is a ring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A saint in a painting, a god with a glowing ring above the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins A to the rest; 'on' sets the ring after the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of the sun, music and prophecy, a deity worshipped across the classical world.

clue.text: Russian navy skirts disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruins and wrecked, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A news line: the Russian navy narrowly avoids a calamity at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' looks like the verb of the surface but is part of the fodder NAVY SKIRTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Stravinsky, composer of The Rite of Spring, was born in Russia, an example of a Russian.

clue.text: Aim to tour round part of Acropolis, having lots of equipment

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go about the gable
to tour is to wander about, so the three letters move around

parts.note: the pediment is the triangular gable of a Greek temple like the Parthenon

explanation.surface: A tourist on the Acropolis weighed down with luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is Latin for baggage, and means cumbersome kit or belongings carried along.

clue.text: No Jew — a painter

parts.note: goy is a Yiddish word for a non-Jewish person

explanation.surface: A statement of someone's background: not Jewish, and an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the great Spanish court artist, an example of a painter.

clue.text: The end of epoch before present

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only the final letter of epoch is used

parts.note: ere is a poetic word meaning before

explanation.surface: A historian's remark: the close of one era came before today.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is in attendance is at this place, so the adverb of place fits being in attendance.

clue.text: Point of card game, not on line — employing memory

indicators.note: employing means taking on, so the computer memory goes to work inside the other letters
not here means without, so the two letters are removed from the game

parts.note: pontoon is a British card game like blackjack or twenty-one
ROM is read-only memory in a computer
RY is short for railway, a railway line

explanation.surface: The point of a game of cards, played without a line but relying on remembering the cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is a British card game like blackjack; 'Point' means a headland, not a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland jutting into the sea is called a point, as in many coastal place names.

clue.text: Allow, at this moment, head to drop

indicators.note: the head of a down word is its top letter, and dropping it sends it to the bottom

parts.note: now means at this moment

explanation.surface: Permission given right now for someone's head to droop.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit or concede a point is to accept it, a sense of allow.

clue.text: Orders at intervals to take time-critical back up

indicators.note: at intervals means every other letter, taking the even letters of the word

parts.note: something time-critical is urgent

explanation.surface: Commands to take back up something pressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rising again after a decline is coming back into strength, rising anew.

clue.text: I had travelled through French region to capital

indicators.note: the short form goes through the region, ending up inside it

parts.note: Provence is the region of south-east France
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A traveller's diary: crossing southern France on the way to the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a joining word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the state capital of Rhode Island in the United States.

clue.text: Casting an eye over contest — good to secure victory

parts.note: to vie is to contest or compete
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: Watching a match where one side needs only a good result to clinch it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at or inspecting something is to cast an eye over it.

clue.text: Unable to move with speed

definitions.meaning: stuck firm, fixed in place, as with a door held tight

explanation.surface: A paradox: being stuck yet going quickly at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both firmly fixed and rapid, two senses of the same word.

clue.text: Seeing political dissenters, fine to start shooting

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a film director calls this word to start the cameras rolling

explanation.surface: Rebels in a party, cleared to open fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeing' and 'to' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakaway group within a party disagreeing with the leadership is a splinter group.

clue.text: Near avoiding cold, but go down

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping away from, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: close means near
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Staying close but out of the chill, yet still going down with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: To go down in a contest is to be beaten in it, the opposite of winning.

clue.text: Window that's in airport not closed

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation within the shortened airport name
not closed means left open at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Orly is an airport of Paris
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A window at a terminal building that is still open.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting bay with a window on an upper floor, especially in old colleges.

clue.text: Scrooge for one I rope into support for prayer

parts.note: Ebenezer Scrooge in Dickens's A Christmas Carol is the classic tightwad
cord is a thin rope

explanation.surface: A tale of tying a skinflint up and dragging him into church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is a joining word here.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge under a tip-up choir seat lets clergy lean while standing through long services.

clue.text: One hunted by sailors in tin vessel

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
an ark is a boat, as Noah's

explanation.surface: Sailors chasing their prey in a metal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a joining word. Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark has a crew sailing in pursuit of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's nonsense poem sends a ship's crew in pursuit of this imaginary creature.

clue.text: Skimpily-dressed servant?

parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt, the skimpy garment
someone dressed has clothes on

explanation.surface: A household servant in a revealing outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Wearing a mini, someone has a mini on; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A subordinate who slavishly serves a master is a lowly follower or lackey.

clue.text: Revolutionary causes securing good patronage

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the reshuffled letters wrap round the pious word
revolutionary means turning over, so the letters of causes are rearranged

parts.note: PI, short for pious, means good

explanation.surface: Political radicals' movements win the backing of a worthy sponsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Under someone's sponsorship or protection is to be under their patronage.

clue.text: Uncle deleting page from contents of in-box?

indicators.note: deleting means removing, so the letter for page is cut out

parts.note: junk email that fills an inbox is spam

explanation.surface: A relative clearing junk out of his email.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the personification of the United States government.

clue.text: Severe criticism about relative status in fleet

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the criticism wraps round the family member

parts.note: flak is heavy criticism, from anti-aircraft fire
a gran, grandmother, is a relative

explanation.surface: Harsh words over who outranks whom in the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirals hold the rank entitling them to fly a flag, the senior status in a navy.

clue.text: Four different notes, or one official one

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
N is the abbreviation for note
ut is the old name for doh, the first note of the scale
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A choice between a jotted set of musical notes and one formal memo.
explanation.walkthrough: Each piece is a different kind of note: two sol-fa names, a letter-named note, and the written abbreviation N.
explanation.definitionFit: The record of a committee meeting is a formal written memo, the official kind of note.
